title: Shortest Unsorted Continuous Subarray
spaceBreakdown:
- int variables (n, maxSeen, right, minSeen, left, i): O(1)
- no containers, no recursion, no heap/stack allocations
- not counted: input vector
approach: An element is already in its correct sorted position if it is ≥ every element to its left and ≤ every element to its right. Scan left-to-right tracking the running maximum: the rightmost index where the current element falls below the running max is the right boundary of the unsorted subarray. Symmetrically, scan right-to-left tracking the running minimum: the leftmost index where the current element exceeds the running min is the left boundary. The answer is `right - left + 1`, or 0 if no element was out of place.
hints: If an element is already in its correct sorted position, what must be true about it relative to every element to its left and every element to its right?

Track the running maximum while scanning left-to-right; the rightmost index where `nums[i]` falls below the running max is the right end. Symmetrically, track the running minimum right-to-left for the left end. In `[2,6,4,8,10,9,15]`, at index 5 the value 9 is below running max 10, so right = 5; at index 1 the value 6 exceeds running min 4, so left = 1.

```
maxSeen = nums[0], right = -1
for i from 1 to n-1:
    if nums[i] < maxSeen: right = i
    else: maxSeen = nums[i]

minSeen = nums[n-1], left = -1
for i from n-2 down to 0:
    if nums[i] > minSeen: left = i
    else: minSeen = nums[i]

if right == -1: return 0
return right - left + 1
```

**Already sorted** - no element is out of place
`Input: [1,2,3,4]` → `Expected: 0`
⚠️ Bug: omitting the `if (right == -1) return 0;` guard → returns 1

**All equal** - every element equals every other
`Input: [5,5,5,5]` → `Expected: 0`
⚠️ Bug: using `<=` instead of `<` in the right-boundary check → returns 4

**All negative, already sorted** - values are negative and ascending
`Input: [-5,-4,-3,-2,-1]` → `Expected: 0`
⚠️ Bug: initializing `maxSeen` to 0 instead of `nums[0]` → every element is below 0, right = 4, left = -1, returns 6

**Reverse sorted** - entire array needs sorting
`Input: [5,4,3,2,1]` → `Expected: 5`
⚠️ Bug: checking `nums[i] > maxSeen` instead of `nums[i] < maxSeen` → right stays -1, returns 0

followUps.q: Return the actual subarray indices [left, right] instead of its length.
followUps.a: Run the same algorithm unchanged. When `right != -1`, return `{left, right}`; otherwise return `{-1, -1}` to signal the array is already sorted. O(n) time, O(1) space.

followUps.q: What if the array arrives as a single-pass data stream with no random access?
followUps.a: You must buffer the entire stream in memory first, because the right-to-left scan requires knowing suffix minimums that are not yet available during a forward-only pass. O(n) time, O(n) space to buffer.

followUps.q: Find the shortest subarray to sort in descending order so the whole array becomes non-increasing.
followUps.a: Invert every comparison: track the running minimum left-to-right for the right boundary (rightmost index where `nums[i] > running min`) and the running maximum right-to-left for the left boundary (leftmost index where `nums[i] < running max`). Same O(n) time, O(1) space.
